title: FIG. 01 · The Room, In Register
summary: Your layout notes, exactly as in X: the statement on two lines near the vertical centre, the lede and both doors at the bottom-right, and the fixed-scope note at the bottom-left. What changes is how the room is seen. Here it is seen through a glass partition of three panes that slide into register as the page loads, an architectural alternative to X's single film. The lede's promise (fragmented growth → repeatable pipeline) becomes the hero's one motion.

reference.site: Round 1 · A + C (hero A 'FIG. 01 · The Room' composition and film; hero C's Atlas-style grid over the picture, made physical and kept below the type)
reference.borrowed: From hero A, nearly everything: the warm frosted room (a height-fit plate, with the man seen from behind, the standing colleague and the seated one), the real nav (lockup, tracked caps, outlined AUDIT REQUEST ↗), the red-square label, the two-voice statement, the red rule, the two doors, the fixed-scope note, and the FIG. 01 band with a segmented control and Pause film. From hero C: the idea of a drawn frame standing between the viewer and the room, plus its registration marks. C's twelve faint column lines are reduced to three glass panes, and the only lines drawn are below the statement.
reference.kelwin: All your layout notes are applied. (1) The statement is on two lines: 'Revenue is an' / 'architectural problem.', 116px Mona wide 430, with 'problem.' in light 300 at --fg-2. (2) It is left-aligned at col 1 and held almost at the vertical centre: its optical centre sits at about 46% of the 816px body. (3) The lede (18px, 3 lines) and the two doors sit at the bottom-right in pane 3 (cols 9–12, where round-1's note was). The lede hangs 24px under the transom, and the red REQUEST A SYSTEM AUDIT ↗ stands over the underlined TALK TO THE TEAM → on the sill floor. (4) '■ A FIXED-SCOPE DIAGNOSTIC · Ten working days. Clear findings. Actionable recommendations.' sits at the bottom-left in pane 1, and its last baseline shares the secondary door's baseline, so both corners finish on one line. Pane 2's sill stays empty, and the seated colleague shows through it. (5) A little of C, under quota: hero X's two + marks where the nav hairline meets the margins (so the bar is identical to X's), the partition linework (one margin-to-margin transom at y 624 in --line-2, whose first 48px is the red rule, plus two mullions on the 4|5 and 8|9 gutters that drop from it to the band), two registration marks on the joints, and one film timecode. Above the transom nothing is drawn: no line crosses the statement or the people, and the panes read only as frost (pane 1 dense, blur 12px and 70% graphite, behind the start of the statement; pane 2 medium, 10px and 34%; pane 3 clear, 8px and 0%, over the man seen from behind). The legibility scrim is therefore the building, not a soft gradient. Red appears only on the primary button, the rule and the two label squares.

motion: entrance: the film fades up (900ms) already slightly out of register. Each pane's pass of the film is offset and at its own scale: pane 1 (−30, +22) ×1.035, pane 2 (+38, −46) ×0.965, pane 3 (−28, +30) ×1.045. Silhouettes jog at the joints the way misregistered print plates do. The nav hairline draws and hero X's two + marks fade in at its ends. The kit's head choreography, shifted by 160ms, runs over the fragmented room: the label fades in, 'Revenue is an' rises, then 'architectural problem.', and the red rule draws. The transom then draws out of the rule, left to right (820ms, 1.1s), and the two mullions drop from it to the band (1.3s, 140ms stagger). The lede and the doors fade up at bottom-right with the note at bottom-left, and the band hairline, caption and controls follow.

orchestrated moment (the morph): at 700ms the partition registers. Each pane's film slides and rescales into register over 1.6s --ease-inout, staggered 140ms left to right, and the room becomes one coherent picture behind the statement. As it locks (≈2.4–2.8s), the two registration marks land on the joints and the control reads REGISTERED. This is C's drafting precision expressed as motion, standing in for the lede: fragmented growth → repeatable system.

ambient: only the film loops: the 32s drift (all three passes stay locked together), a silhouette crossing, and the frosted-glass grain. The timecode advances with the film (one change per second) and stops when it is paused. Nothing else moves.

interaction: FRAGMENTED | REGISTERED slides the panes out of and back into register (1.6s ease-inout, 140ms stagger). The joint marks fade out at once on Fragmented and land again 1.7s after Registered. 'PAUSE FILM' really pauses all three passes of the film, the walker, the grain and the timecode, and flips to 'PLAY FILM'. Kit hovers apply on the doors, the outlined AUDIT REQUEST and the nav items.

on the live site: one background <video> is drawn into a <canvas> in three pane slices (drawImage per pane with its offset, scale and ctx.filter blur), or three muted <video> elements on one source are kept in sync. The registration runs once, on load. Reduced motion shows the registered resting frame with no entrance, and the timecode holds still.
notes: The stage is 1000px: 96 nav + 816 body (528 room + 288 sill) + 88 band. It is 40px taller than X, because pane 3 is four columns (422px). The doors must stack there (side by side they need ~529px), and the sill has to hold the lede, the gap and both doors. The rows are fixed so that the rule and the transom land together at y 624. That is where the joints, their marks and the mullions are keyed. The lede is 18px, the low end of the hero spec's 18–20px, so it stays at three lines in pane 3. X (literal) and Y (architectural) share your layout but differ in composition. X has a free-floating action block across cols 8–12 with side-by-side doors, corner marks, a ruler and a Close → Wide pull-back. Y has three equal glass panes, a built sill with an open middle pane, a narrow corner block with stacked doors, and a registration morph. Earlier review changes: a previous Y broke three of your notes (the lede was bottom-left, the note bottom-centre, the statement at 59%) and ran full-height mullions through the statement and over the people, which DIRECTION-AC §3.4 bans. Both problems are fixed. The fragment offsets were halved so the entrance reads as misregistration, not a glitch collage. The plate is the shared mirrored stand-in; its mirrored half only shows dimly under pane 1's dense frost, and the live video is not mirrored. The fragmented state can be checked by clicking FRAGMENTED. This pass: the bar now carries hero X's two + marks at the hairline ends, so the nav is identical to X's (lockup, items, outlined AUDIT REQUEST, hairline and marks were measured to the pixel). The build was also refreshed onto the fixed kit: the selected FRAGMENTED button had rendered blank under the pointer, and it now reads graphite on paper.
addressed: 'Two lines rather than three' → 'Revenue is an / architectural problem.'
'Almost vertically centre the heading, left-aligned' → its optical centre sits at about 46% of the body, at col 1.
'Move the subtext and both CTAs to the bottom-right' → the lede, Request a System Audit and Talk to the team stand in the right-hand pane.
'Move A fixed-scope diagnostic to the bottom-left' → it sits in the left-hand pane, and its last line shares the secondary door's baseline.
'A little of the observed room, not too much' → three touches: + marks, a drawn sill (one transom, two mullions) and a timecode.
'Better ideas welcome' → the room is seen through three glass panes that slide into register on load: fragmented growth becoming one system.
